evidence.clarity: 1440 and 390: h1 'Sort the swap before your break is over.' plus a lede that names nurses posting/picking up swaps, skill mix and hours checks, and manager approve/decline in one tap; fine print under the CTAs names the buyer (nurse managers, directors of nursing). The headline speaks to nurses while the only action is for managers, so the 'who' shifts between headline and CTA.
evidence.fit: Tone fits the 12-hour shift: phone status bar '03:14 / Break · 22 min left', the '06:45 "oh, we swapped"' card, a timeline 'inside a single night shift'. Brief constraints get a dedicated 'What Swaptide doesn't do' section (manager decides, union agreements untouched, no payroll) and an honest pilot box. Nurses get the hero headline and timeline but no path of their own; the manager section is a static picture.
evidence.distinctiveness: Structure is the stock kit: pill eyebrow, split hero with phone mockup, three-card 'what it replaces' row, dark steps band, icon-list feature column, three-column 'doesn't do' grid, FAQ accordion, centred CTA band. Product-specific touches (break timer in status bar, 06:45 card, night-shift track) sit inside that template; the night-shift track's markers are decoration with no labels.
evidence.proof: 1440: a phone mockup of one swap with three passed checks and 'Sent to Marisol (unit manager)' is in the first screen, and a manager queue with one flagged request appears in the #rules section. But the hero phone (Priya R., Dana K., Marisol, '4 West', '36 → 48.5 h') and the manager queue are never labelled as examples anywhere on the page, and 'Posting and picking up a swap takes a couple of minutes on a phone' is asserted without basis.
evidence.interaction: 1440/768/390: 'See how a swap moves' scrolls to #how, all five 'Book a pilot call' links go to https://swaptide.example/pilot, FAQ details open/close, no console errors. evidence.clarity: 1440/768/390: h1 'Every swap reaches you before the shift does' plus the bold line 'Swaptide is a shift-swap app for hospital nursing units.' and the one-tap approve/decline sentence say what it is, who it's for (the manager as 'you') and the next step ('Book a pilot call', with a note that the call covers your unit's swap rules and whether a pilot fits).
evidence.fit: The demo, the 'You set the limits' rulesheet ('Enter the skill-mix and hours limits from your unit policy and union agreement'), and the Q&A ('Does it override our union agreement? No... doesn't decide for you'; 'Does it handle payroll? No') resolve every constraint in what the page does, not just what it says. The 12-hour shift is built into the roster (D 07:00–19:30, N 19:00–07:30), the night/day band and the '19:00 · HANDOFF' close. The nurse audience is thinner: one 'For nurses on the unit' line that is hidden below 1000px, plus the timeline story.
evidence.distinctiveness: The hero artifact is a unit roster grid with D/N cells, a 'posted' Sat night and a 'N?' pending cell, which reads as a nursing schedule rather than a SaaS card. Also a drawn break-room whiteboard with numbered problem pins, a 24-hour night/day band, and a 4 North floor plan locating break room, station and manager's office. Condensed Heros type reads as signage/timetable. You would recognise it without the logo. Minor: the whiteboard 'handwriting' is set in the same condensed sans, so it reads typeset.
evidence.proof: 1440: the operable 'Try one swap' board sits in the first viewport (top 328px). Tapping Dana flags '4th night in a row. Unit limit: 3.' with an orange run underline across Wed–Sat; Marcus flags skill mix and highlights 'Also on Sat night: Ken M., Ana S. Neither is charge-qualified.' Week hours update (36→48). This answers the manager's main doubt (does it catch rule breaks before me). Minor inconsistency: the queue is labelled 'sample week of 8 Nov' but lists 13, 14 and 19 Nov.
evidence.craft: Deliberate type scale (condensed display, Heros text), 8px spacing tokens, 1.5px ink borders used consistently on the board, rulesheet and status box, axe clean, smallest text 12px. All operated states (pending, flag, approved with strikethrough 'off', declined) render cleanly at 1440/768/390. Weak spots: the 1440 hero is dense with a floating 'Status: in pilot' box and dead space beside the h1, and the section padding (120px) makes the middle feel long.
evidence.mobile: 390: recomposed. Menu button opens a full-width list (Escape and link tap both close it; tapped 'For nurse managers', it went to #managers and the menu hid). The roster fits without overflow, all targets 44–50px. After tapping 'Marcus T.' (y 352), the verdict updates at y 497 in the same viewport, with Approve at y 792. Downsides: the board starts at y 516 and is 951px tall, so only its header is in the first screen; the nurse line and floor plan are hidden on phones; stepper feedback (queue-status) sits ~326px below the steppers.
evidence.honesty: Board header: 'Sample unit, names and week, written for this page', visible at 390; 'Sample, set by the manager' on the rulesheet; 'Your queue, sample week of 8 Nov'; '4 North, sample plan, not to scale'; the footer repeats it. Pilot status is in the first screen at both widths ('Status: in pilot' box at 1440, the CTA note at 390). The Q&A says no results will be quoted. The demo's Approve/Decline are framed as 'The manager's tap. A flag informs the call; it doesn't make it.'
evidence.interaction: Operated at 1440, 768 and 390: radio labels Jo/Dana/Marcus each re-render roster, checks and verdict. Approve shows 'Approved... flag noted' and moves the shift (Priya's Sat struck 'off', her week drops to 24). Approving again gives 'Already approved. Pick someone else or Reset'. Decline after approve shows 'Priya R. keeps Sat night'. Reset returns to Jo. Steppers flag queue items live ('3rd shift in a row, over your limit of 2'). Past the bounds it shows 'Sample range is 2 to 4 in a row.' No console errors.
evidence.copy: Specific nouns from the unit: '“Kid’s recital Saturday at 18:30. Anyone want my night?”', 'between the 02:00 and 04:00 rounds', 'What your director, your union rep and your IT team will ask', 'on the phone already in a scrub pocket'. Buttons say what happens. Microcopy is written, not defaulted. A few lines are awkward ('a swap reaches you after someone has worked it').
evidence.first_screen: 1440: one viewport holds the specific outcome for the manager, the pilot status, the CTA and a fully operable, labelled sample swap. 390: promise, the pilot note and the CTA are in view, but only the board's title and the first lines of the sample show before scrolling.

problems: The nurse audience is thin and loses its one hero line on phones (.hero-nurse is display:none below 1000px), which is where nurses would read it.
At 390 the demo starts at y 516 and is a 951px-tall block, so promise and artifact do not share the first screen, and stepper feedback lands well below the steppers.
The 1440 hero is dense, with a floating status box and dead space; the whiteboard's typeset 'handwriting' and the queue's week label not matching its dates (8 Nov vs 13–19 Nov) are small lapses.

reason: B shows the product's core job early, in a form that belongs to nursing: a roster you can operate in the first screen. Its states, labels and copy are consistent, and every brief constraint is made visible in the demo itself. A is a clean, well-toned but templated page whose artifact is a static, unlabelled mockup with dead-looking buttons and weaker mobile. I would change my mind only if the nurse-on-a-break audience were weighted above the buying manager, since A's headline speaks to nurses more directly.
